Overview

Saint Kitts and Nevis at a Glance

Saint Kitts and Nevis is a two-island federation with a common law legal system, the Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court as its superior court and the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council as its final court of appeal. Company law differs between the islands: companies in Saint Kitts are formed under the Companies Act, while Nevis has its own corporate legislation, including the Nevis Island Business Corporation Ordinance, and a long-established international financial services sector. Registration involves the Financial Services Regulatory Commission and the Registrar of Companies. For investigators, the federation's structure means confirming at the outset which island and which statute govern an entity, and recognising that public access to ownership information is limited.

Organisations commission investigative work involving Saint Kitts and Nevis for two main reasons. First, Nevis companies, limited liability companies and trusts appear in international ownership structures, so litigants, lenders and compliance teams need to understand who stands behind them. Second, the federation operates one of the longest-running citizenship by investment programmes, and employers, banks, counterparties and courts sometimes need to understand the background of individuals holding second citizenship. Other exposures arise in tourism and real estate development, the ship registry and international education. Typical matters include asset tracing in fraud and insolvency cases, enhanced due diligence on investors and verification of claimed business histories.

Typical Matters

Where Investigative Work Involving Saint Kitts and Nevis Concentrates

01

Nevis entity ownership research

Identifying the people and assets behind Nevis corporations, LLCs and trusts that appear in fraud, insolvency, divorce or commercial disputes, using registry confirmations, litigation in the Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court and other courts, foreign filings and media, and supporting counsel seeking disclosure orders.

02

Economic citizen background checks

Enhanced due diligence on individuals who hold Saint Kitts and Nevis citizenship by investment alongside other nationalities, examining identity history, prior names, business record, litigation, sanctions exposure and media in the jurisdictions where they actually live and work.

03

Asset tracing in fraud matters

Supporting victims and insolvency practitioners pursuing assets routed through federation entities, combining corporate genealogy, transaction analysis from client records, real estate research and coordination with Eastern Caribbean counsel on freezing and disclosure applications.

04

Real estate and project counterparties

Background research on developers, sponsors and contractors in tourism and real estate projects, including those approved for investment programmes, covering corporate history, prior projects, litigation and financial difficulties, for lenders, purchasers and partners.

05

Ship registry and maritime diligence

Research on owners and managers of vessels flagged or previously flagged in the federation's ship registry, including ownership changes, related companies and adverse media, to support charterers, insurers and compliance teams evaluating maritime counterparties.

Law & Regulation

What applies before any work touching Saint Kitts and Nevis begins

Legal system

Saint Kitts and Nevis has a common law legal system derived from English law. The Supreme Court of Judicature, established under the Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court arrangements shared with other OECS states, comprises the High Court and the Eastern Caribbean Court of Appeal; final appeals lie to the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council in London. The Caribbean Court of Justice has original jurisdiction on CARICOM treaty matters but no appellate jurisdiction. Arbitration is governed by the Arbitration Act (Cap. 3.01), and the Court of Appeal also offers mediation.

Data protection

Data Protection Act, 2018 (passed May 2018; commencement order not identified) · Regulator: None identified; the Act is reported as not yet in force

Saint Kitts and Nevis passed a Data Protection Act in May 2018, published in the Official Gazette in June 2018, but it comes into force only on a date fixed by ministerial order, and a University of the West Indies review reported no commencement order as of February 2025. No supervisory authority has been identified. As of 2024, the US State Department reported no measures restricting companies from transmitting customer data abroad. Investigations collecting personal information in the federation should still follow the Act's principles of lawful and limited processing, constitutional protections and the common law of confidence. TDSC confirms data handling with local counsel where personal data will be collected locally.

Private investigators

We have not identified, from official sources available to us, a dedicated licensing regime for private investigators in Saint Kitts and Nevis. The legal position of private investigative activity, including surveillance, recording and approaches to witnesses, should be confirmed with local counsel before any step is taken locally. In a small jurisdiction, discretion is essential and inquiries can quickly become known. TDSC therefore relies principally on documentary and open-source research conducted from Nashville and, where local work is required, coordinates appropriately qualified professionals within limits agreed with counsel.

Corporate & public records

Companies in Saint Kitts are incorporated under the Companies Act (Cap. 21.03) and companies in Nevis under the Nevis Business Corporation Ordinance, with other Nevis legislation governing limited liability companies and trusts. The Financial Services Regulatory Commission supervises registered entities on each island. Companies must keep shareholder registers and accounting records, and regulated service providers must identify and verify beneficial owners, but we have not identified a public beneficial ownership register; documents filed with the Saint Kitts Registrar may be inspected for a fee. Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court judgments are published, and ownership questions often turn on court disclosure orders.

Anti-corruption & AML

The Anti-Corruption Act, No. 5 of 2023, assented in April 2023, creates special offences of abuse of office, bribery and trading in influence, extends to bribery of foreign officials and establishes an Office of the Special Prosecutor; it takes effect on a date fixed by order. The Integrity in Public Life Act sets a code of conduct and declarations of interest for officials. Anti-money laundering obligations rest on the Proceeds of Crime Act and 2011 regulations, enforced with the Financial Intelligence Unit, the police and the Director of Public Prosecutions.

Engagement Standard

How TDSC Scopes Matters Touching Saint Kitts and Nevis

TDSC scopes engagements touching Saint Kitts and Nevis from Nashville and begins by establishing which island's legislation governs each entity, since Saint Kitts and Nevis maintain separate corporate regimes. Research relies on registry confirmations, published Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court and Privy Council judgments, foreign corporate and court filings, property and maritime records and media. Because ownership information is generally held by registered agents rather than publicly, TDSC works with counsel where a disclosure order or other court process is the lawful route to it. Any local inquiry is discreet, agreed with counsel and carried out by appropriately qualified professionals. Personal data is handled consistently with the principles of the Data Protection Act 2018 and minimised throughout. TDSC does not provide legal advice.

TDSC has no office in Saint Kitts and Nevis. Engagements are directed from Nashville, Tennessee; where work on the ground is needed, it is performed by appropriately licensed local professionals under a written scope. TDSC does not provide legal advice.

Questions

Saint Kitts and Nevis: Frequently Asked Questions

Can you find out who owns a Nevis LLC?

Not usually from public registries alone, which confirm existence and the registered agent but rarely ownership. We build a picture from litigation, foreign filings, transaction records available to the client, property and media sources. Where a definitive answer is needed, counsel may seek a disclosure order from the court, and we support that application with evidence.

What can be verified about someone with Saint Kitts and Nevis citizenship by investment?

Government programme files are not public and we do not seek access to them. We research the person's identity history, business activity, litigation, sanctions exposure and media coverage, mainly in the countries where they live and operate. Second citizenship is lawful; the purpose is to understand the full background of the individual.

Which court hears commercial disputes in the federation?

The High Court of the Eastern Caribbean Supreme Court hears commercial disputes at first instance, with appeals to the Eastern Caribbean Court of Appeal and, finally, the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council. Many judgments are published, which makes court records a useful source for background and ownership research.

Does Saint Kitts and Nevis restrict sending personal data abroad?

As of 2024, the US State Department reported no measures restricting companies from transmitting customer data abroad. The Data Protection Act 2018 has been passed but is reported as not yet brought into force by ministerial order. TDSC nonetheless follows its principles, limits collection to what the matter requires and confirms handling with local counsel where data is gathered locally.

Will TDSC send investigators to Saint Kitts or Nevis?

Only where a local step is genuinely needed and lawful. We have not identified a dedicated investigator licensing regime, and in a small community inquiries are quickly noticed. Most questions can be answered through records and open sources. Where they cannot, local work is planned with counsel and carried out by qualified professionals.
